newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - MARCH 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - MARCH 11.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--The government is considering taking further economic measures this month if tax revenue rates fail to live up to budget forecasts. February's rates, which fell short of targets by more than half, has caused intense concern and National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou is planning meetings this week with officials to see what measures can be taken.

--The significant inflows of new capital noted over the last few days in development mutual funds and the stock exchange has confirmed the demand for alternative investment options following the reduction of returns from bank deposits and state titles.
--Greece's telecoms organisation OTE is promoting an additional 150 billion drachma investment programme aimed at the move to digital systems and increased investment in new technologies.
--Sales of new cars may reach a five-year record this year, if figures for the first two-month period are anything to go on.

--Despite deposit interest rates falling to the lowest levels in 20 years, lending interest rates are still at levels that make it almost prohibitive for business to take out loans. Representatives of four major banks however say the differeence is due to external parameters.
--Deputy Finance Minister George Drys says tax evaders may have to face jail under tough new guidelines to stamp out the phenomenon.

--The imminent new OTE share offer, as well as those of other public organisations and utilities, in combination with a new fall in interest rates, has created optimism about a further rise in prices on the stock exchange. At the same time, senior banking officials say that the rapid changes in trends on the bourse over the past two weeks shows that the Athens stock exchange has not yet matured.
